children: Major asset classes have witnessed significant price swings in recent months, delivering sharply different returns across investment periods.
A comparison of gold and silver, Bitcoin and Ethereum, and the Sensex and Nifty 50 highlights how precious metals, cryptocurrencies and equities have performed over different timeframes.

Bitcoin led the three-month and three-year performance, while silver also delivered strong returns over one and three years. Gold recorded solid gains over the longer term despite recent corrections, while the Sensex and Nifty 50 faced sustained pressure over the shorter investment periods.
Bitcoin and silver lead three-year returns, while equities lag
Here’s how major asset prices moved as of October 7, 2026.

Among precious metals, gold gave positive returns over one year at 20.92 percent and 161.14 percent over three years. Silver’s growth in one year stood at 42.18 percent, with a three-year CAGR of 47.91 percent. However, both metals have faced price corrections over the past one to six months.

On the contrary, the traditional equity market has delivered weaker returns. The Sensex fell 12.45 percent over one year, while its 93-year CAGR stood at just 2.75 percent. The Nifty 50 also declined 11.24 percent over one year and 7.36 percent over six months, although its three-year CAGR of 4.19 percent indicates modest long-term growth.

For cryptocurrency investors, Minal Thukral, Executive VP–Growth & Crypto Business Head at CoinDCX, noted that Bitcoin's long-term performance is strong. He suggests investors need an allocation they can hold through sharp falls, not just one they’re comfortable with when prices are rising.

Their one-year returns are also negative, indicating a challenging period for equities and cryptocurrencies. Overall, the table highlights the relative resilience of gold and silver over the past year, with silver leading returns, while equities and cryptocurrencies have faced greater near-term pressure.
What did a Rs 10,000 SIP return in 1 year?
Further analysis shows how a Rs 10,000 SIP invested across gold, silver, Sensex, Nifty50, Bitcoin, and Ethereum performed over one year.

For cryptocurrency investors, a monthly SIP of Rs 10,000 in Bitcoin would have grown to Rs 1,31,598 over one year, compared with the total investment of Rs 1,20,000. Ethereum recorded the highest value among the listed assets at Rs 37,049 in one year.

“A SIP spreads out the purchases. Those historical returns aren’t a forecast. It’s also worth checking the allocation after a strong rally. Even if the monthly SIP hasn’t changed, Bitcoin may now account for a much larger share of the portfolio than originally intended,” Thukral said.

Among precious metals, a monthly SIP of Rs 10,000 in gold would have grown to Rs 1,24,483 over one year. However, the yellow metal’s short-term returns are below the investment value. Silver’s one-year value rose to Rs 1,21,516, but its short-term investment value also fell below the total contribution.

“Precious metals have seen some near-term correction. However, their medium- to long-term performance remains strong. Silver has outperformed gold significantly. The correction suggests some profit-booking after a strong rally, but the broader performance indicates that precious metals have delivered substantial returns over the longer term,” Nirpendra Yadav, Senior Research Analyst at Bonanza Portfolio, said.

The traditional equity market delivered comparatively weaker results than other major assets. A monthly SIP of Rs 10,000 tracking the Sensex would have accumulated to Rs 1,08,161 over one year, while the same investment tracking the Nifty 50 would have grown to Rs 1,08,405.

Overall, returns from major assets highlight the relative resilience of gold and silver over the past year, with silver leading returns, while equities and cryptocurrencies have faced greater near-term pressure.
